extracted.intended_audience: broadcast and utility applicants, and their legal/engineering representatives participating in FCC/FPC administrative proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Official Federal Register orders designating mutually‑exclusive broadcast applications for consolidated hearing and specifying the substantive and procedural issues (technical, financial, comparative, notice/appearance requirements) applicants must address; also orders providing for hearings/suspension of proposed rate changes for regulated natural gas companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual exclusivity / mutually destructive interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are mutually exclusive where operation as proposed would result in mutually destructive interference; such applications cannot be granted without designation for hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicants’ proposed operations would interfere with one another, the Commission is unable to make the statutory public interest finding and will designate the applications for consolidated hearing (section 309(e) cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative evaluation based on 1 mv/m contours and availability of other FM services
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare areas and populations within the 1 mv/m contours and consider availability of other FM services of 1 mv/m or greater intensity when determining comparative preference among mutually exclusive FM applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purposes of comparison, the areas/populations within the 1 mv/m contours together with other FM service availability will be considered under the standard comparative issue to determine whether a comparative preference should accrue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program duplication (amount and admissible showing)
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicants differ substantially in the amount of AM programming duplicated, evidence regarding program duplication is admissible under the standard comparative issue, but is limited in scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If duplicated programming is proposed (e.g., Glenn West proposes ~two‑thirds duplicated programming while others propose independent operations), the showing permitted is limited to evidence concerning the benefits to be derived from the proposed duplication; a full comparison of program proposals is not permitted absent a specific programming inquiry (Jones T. Sudbury citation).

rubrics_metrics.name: General qualification to construct and operate
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be qualified to construct and operate the proposed station; qualification is a prerequisite but may not resolve mutual exclusivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where applicants are qualified, mutual exclusivity can prevent the Commission from making the public interest finding without a hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial qualification — bank loan terms must be specified
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant relying on a bank loan must provide the loan terms (repayment/interest) so the exact amount of available cash can be determined; conditional or unsigned loan commitments are insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed loans that lack repayment/interest terms, are conditional, or lack guarantor statements do not meet the requirements of FCC Form 301 (section III, paragraph 4(h)). The Commission requires evidence of the actual availability of funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial qualification — guaranty and collateral documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a loan is to be personally guaranteed, the guarantor must submit a statement of willingness to guarantee and documentation (e.g., balance sheet) showing ability to provide required collateral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a bank loan is conditioned on a personal guaranty and collateral, evidence must show what collateral is acceptable and that the guarantor has the ability to supply it; unsigned/unsupported guarantees are inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial qualification — balance sheet liquidity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must demonstrate liquid and current assets in excess of current liabilities available to finance construction and first‑year operations, as defined in section III, paragraph 4(d) of FCC Form 301.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance sheets must segregate current liabilities as required; without this, the Commission cannot determine whether liquid assets are available for construction and first‑year operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial qualification — sponsor (third‑party) loan commitments and assets
rubrics_metrics.description: If relying on a sponsor or principal (e.g., A. Richard Cohen) to lend funds (e.g., $250,000), the sponsor must execute loan agreements and provide financial statements showing liquid/current assets in excess of current liabilities sufficient to meet the commitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsigned commitments or absent financial statements from the sponsor do not satisfy the Commission’s requirement to establish availability of funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial qualification — revenue estimates and support
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants claiming future revenues to supplement funds must provide supporting information that demonstrates the soundness of the revenue estimate (Ultravision Broadcasting standard).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitted information must adequately support the estimate; unsupported or insufficient revenue projections will lead to specification of financial issues for hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial qualification — availability of other sources of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: If revenue will not suffice, the applicant must show other sources of funds sufficient to meet cash requirements for construction and first‑year operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission will consider alternative funding sources in determining financial qualification; absence of demonstrated alternate sources raises financial issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification of discrete financial hearing issues (items a–h)
rubrics_metrics.description: When financial qualifications are in doubt, the Commission may specify discrete issues for hearing such as: terms of a named bank loan; amount of additional cash needed; nature of collateral; sponsor’s ability to provide collateral; availability of liquid assets; whether sponsor will undertake a loan and has sufficient assets; sufficiency of revenues; whether the applicant is financially qualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These discrete issues mirror the precise factual showings the applicant must make at hearing to establish financial qualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative determination of public interest and grantability
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated hearing issues include determining which proposal best serves the public interest and, based on the evidence adduced, which application for construction permit should be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the substantive comparative questions the hearing will resolve after considering technical, financial, programming, and service‑area evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficiency of frequency use assessed by Grade B contour disparities
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant disparities in proposed Grade B contours among applicants permit introduction of evidence as to which proposal would represent a more efficient use of the frequency under the comparative issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engineering comparisons of coverage contours are a metric for comparative preference; Commission policy cited (Harriscope) supports this consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main studio location — good cause and public interest standard (§73.613(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests to locate main studios outside the principal community will be granted only upon a showing of good cause and a finding that the proposed location would not be inconsistent with operation of the station in the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where good cause is shown (e.g., combined studio–transmitter at short distance), Commission consent under §73.613(b) may be provided; conditioned on grant and public interest determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliation/ownership concerns (CATV operations) may affect grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Ownership interests (e.g., operation of CATV systems by a subsidiary) may render a grant subject to further action pending separate Commission inquiries into ownership patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants may be made 'without prejudice' to outcomes of separate proceedings (Docket No. 17371), preserving Commission flexibility to act on broader ownership issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirement — filing written appearance within 20 days (§1.221(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: To avail themselves of the opportunity to be heard, applicants must file in triplicate a written appearance stating intent to appear and present evidence on the specified issues within twenty (20) days of mailing of the order, in person or by attorney, pursuant to §1.221(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely file the required written appearance may forfeit opportunity to present evidence at the hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirement — notice of hearing publication (§311(a)(2), §1.594, §1.594(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must give notice of the hearing individually or jointly, within the time and manner prescribed by §1.594, and advise the Commission of publication as required by §1.594(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with statutory and rule notice requirements is mandatory to effectuate public notice of hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to correct inaccurate technical information / permissibility of corrective amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are required to furnish accurate technical information; if they discover errors they have a duty to appropriately amend; corrective amendments that merely correct descriptive errors (e.g., site elevation) are permissible and applicants have no vested rights in their errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opponents who believe amended representations are in error may initiate inquiry by available procedures; public interest is not served by conducting hearings based on facts the applicant believes to be false.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for hearing on rate filings (FPC): unjust, unreasonable, unduly discriminatory, preferential, or otherwise unlawful
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed changes in rates/charges may be subject to hearing if they may be unjust, unreasonable, unduly discriminatory, preferential, or otherwise unlawful under the Natural Gas Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission will initiate public hearings under sections 4 and 15 of the Natural Gas Act and related rules when such concerns are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension and deferral of proposed rate supplements pending hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending hearings and decisions, the Commission may suspend proposed rate supplements and defer their use until a specified 'Date Suspended Until' and until made effective as prescribed by the Natural Gas Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension periods (e.g., five months) are set consistent with statutory notice periods and may prevent respondents from putting rates into effect pending review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention and petition to intervene filing deadlines and rules (18 CFR 1.8 and 1.37(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of intervention or petitions to intervene in rate proceedings must be filed with the Federal Power Commission by specified dates and in accordance with the rules of practice (18 CFR 1.8 and 1.37(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order specifies the filing address and deadline (e.g., on or before February 15, 1968) for intervention requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition allowing rate filings to become effective subject to refund upon filing of undertakings
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate filings may be permitted to become effective subject to refund if respondents, within a specified period (e.g., 20 days), execute and file agreements/undertakings to comply with refunding and reporting procedures (per Natural Gas Act and §154.102).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing must be accompanied by certificate showing service upon purchasers; unless advised otherwise within 15 days, such undertakings are deemed accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with area increased rate ceilings and policy No. 61‑1
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed increased rates that exceed applicable area increased rate ceilings (per Commission statement of general policy No. 61‑1, as amended) justify suspension or other remedial action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission compares proposed rates to area ceilings (e.g., 11 cents/Mcf, 12.7 cents/Mcf) and treats filings exceeding ceilings as requiring suspension and hearings; special handling may apply for tax reimbursement‑related increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date determination under filing moratoriums
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a filing moratorium is in effect, proposed filings may be treated as though filed on the moratorium expiration date (e.g., treated as filed Jan. 1, 1968) for suspension/timing purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This affects suspension period calculations (e.g., suspending rates for five months from statutory notice expiration).
